At 0% progress, prioritize one inexpensive, falsifiable model change: a recent-history residual added to SASRec’s final representation. No improvement is established yet.

**Insights and directions.**

1. User feedback favors recent behavior and repeated narrow preferences. This motivates testing recency explicitly, without claiming to recover true intent.
2. Current probes measure sampled training separation and embedding alignment. Neither establishes validation ranking quality, so preserve official macro HR@10 as the selection criterion.
3. Missing metadata and empty batches weaken existing diagnostics. Return unavailable values with counts, and restore the model’s original training mode after probing.
4. Shuffling studies question whether recommendation benchmarks require sequence order [1]. Compare recency aggregation with the Transformer before adding more complex sequence machinery.
5. Reproducibility findings show that configuration can change architecture comparisons [2]. Hold training settings fixed while introducing one residual component.
6. Sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model rankings [3]. Keep the pinned evaluator authoritative and label full-catalog observations separately.

These insights suggest three directions: simple recency modeling, controlled sensitivity diagnostics, and explicit uncertainty about unobserved product relationships.

**Framework.**

| Component | Observable evidence | Supported conclusion | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| SASRec | Ordered interactions | Learned sequence associations | Current intent |
| Recent-item mean | Last observed interactions | Recent preference signal | Purchase necessity |
| Perturbation probes | Paired output changes | Sensitivity to history | Causal explanation |
| Title/specification audit | Explicit text spans | Documented relationships | Ownership and compatibility when unspecified |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recent-history residual [1,2] | 4/7/2 | Cheap, direct test of recency | May amplify already satisfied needs |
| Matched recent/older removal probes [1] | 4/7/3 | Tests reliance on different history regions | Removal changes positions and length |
| Abstaining specification audit [4] | 6/6/6 | Makes evidence inspectable | Sparse specifications limit coverage |

**Selected algorithm.** Let `h` be SASRec’s final valid-position feature and `r` the mean embedding of the last five nonpadding items. Score item `i` as `dot(h + alpha*r, embedding[i])`. Freeze the trained SASRec checkpoint initially; select a separate scalar per dataset from `alpha ∈ {0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2}` using pinned validation HR@10. Including zero permits retaining the baseline; all comparisons consume the shared budget.

```python
for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    model = load_baseline_checkpoint(dataset)
    for alpha in [0.0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2]:
        scores = score_with_recent_residual(model, alpha, recent_count=5)
        record_pinned_validation_hits(dataset, alpha, scores)
    save_selected_alpha_and_checkpoint(dataset)
```

Persist the residual configuration and implement identical scoring in the predictor writer. Preserve dataset routing, seeds, splits, and `DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']`. Adapt diagnostic scoring to use the same residual causally at every sequence position; retain `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` and `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)`.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008), [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03873), [3](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651), [4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7075849/).

idea.description: Add a validation-selected recent-history embedding residual to each dataset’s SASRec representation, starting with frozen model weights.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback identifies insufficient emphasis on recent, specific behavior. An additive residual tests this hypothesis with a small implementation and includes the unchanged baseline as alpha=0.
idea.implementation_notes: Use the existing preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment default 200. Build recent means only from observed prefix items, excluding padding. For sequence-position diagnostics, compute the last-five mean independently for each causal prefix; never include future positives. Preserve embedding scaling consistently between training-side scoring and exported inference. Save alpha, recent_count, architecture configuration, item mappings, and checkpoint beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer and all four dataset routes. Diagnosis must inspect view.model, restore its previous training mode in finally, return metrics and metric_definitions, and mark empty measurements unavailable with explicit counts. Do not interpret missing interactions as dislike or text similarity as verified compatibility. The supplied material does not include the baseline implementation, so the algorithm is specified as pseudocode rather than an executable replacement train.py.
idea.pseudocode:
def residual_features(sequence, sasrec_features, item_emb, alpha, k=5):
    # Apply independently to every causal prefix for B x L diagnostics.
    recent = causal_last_k_nonpadding_embedding_mean(sequence, item_emb, k)
    return sasrec_features + alpha * recent

for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    model = load_trained_sasrec(dataset)
    # Freeze checkpoint; preserve pinned validation users and candidates.
    for alpha in (0.0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2):
        features = residual_features(sequence, model.log2feats(sequence), model.item_emb, alpha)
        scores = dot_with_candidate_embeddings(final_valid(features), candidates)
        hits[alpha] = pinned_validation_hits(scores)
    best_alpha = argmax_with_smallest_alpha_tiebreak(hits)
    save_trial_artifacts(model, best_alpha, recent_count=5)
    write_predictor_with_identical_scoring(dataset, best_alpha, recent_count=5)
# Official selection remains macro validation HR@10 over all four datasets.

originality.positive: Combines a standard sequential representation with an explicit, directly testable recent-history component.
originality.negative: Embedding averaging and residual score mixtures are established techniques; the proposal is primarily an empirical adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Provides a low-cost foundation for testing when recent behavior adds useful information beyond SASRec.
future_potential.negative: Benefits may depend on sampled evaluation and may not address compatibility or already satisfied needs.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a masked recent mean, one scalar per dataset, configuration persistence, and matching exported scoring.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal position-wise diagnostics and exact feature-scaling parity require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? An Analysis of Datasets for Evaluation of Sequential Recommendations
contributions: Uses interaction shuffling to examine whether benchmark performance depends on sequence order.
limitations: Shuffling sensitivity does not establish users’ true intent or explain individual recommendation errors.

related_work.title: Sequential recommendation reproducibility study
contributions: The supplied summary reports that SASRec versus GRU4Rec comparisons depend strongly on configuration and parameter count.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed recent-history residual improves these four datasets.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics, including model-order reversals.
limitations: Does not provide grounds for replacing the task’s pinned evaluator.

related_work.title: Snorkel: Rapid Training Data Creation with Weak Supervision
contributions: Provides labeling functions that vote or abstain and methods for combining noisy supervision.
limitations: Heuristic product audits would need separate validation and cannot establish compatibility when evidence is missing.
